doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

title: The studio business is gone; technology and playing live
summary: Bucky says studio work disappeared with internet downloads and streaming, and he prefers playing live.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Do you have a sense of what the studio thing is like now?
It’s gone. The studio thing is gone. They make records, but you can buy any record you want cheaper on the internet. You know what I mean?
That’s right. That put us out of business. You play in a nightclub and they have something that they call streaming. It goes all over the country.
That’s right. You mentioned Small’s, that club?
You can get on at night and you can watch who’s playing there, from wherever you are. Well do you think technology has been a blessing or a curse?
Yeah, that’s right. If you don’t play a record date and you play a gig, like I did last night, I enjoy doing that more than I do a record date, playing live.
But you took, what was it a couple of hours, the gig was, two or three hours?
That’s all. Two hours last night.
But you had to leave an hour and a half before it started.
Oh yeah, the weather was bad last night.
Okay. But that’s part of the life, right?
